sentences.text: Food.com recipes come from the Kaggle upload `irkaal/foodcom-recipes-and-reviews` (downloaded 2026-10-20, recipes file sha256 `9f591abe9f8d1c69`), which declares licence CC0-1.0; the declaration is the uploader's, the underlying text is scraped Food.com user content, the uploader's authority to dedicate it is NOT verified, so use is derived/analysis only with no redistribution of text until a human licence review (H2) has ruled.
The corpus has 522,517 recipes and 4,129,433 ingredient part strings; reviews were not downloaded.

No Food.com quantity string contains a letter (0 of 4,583,725 non-null strings), so the unit drop is in the source, not in the parser: 95.166 % of lines carry a bare count and no unit, the parser recognises a unit on only 0.198 % of lines and 4.244 % of food-name strings contain a unit word.
Consequently every Food.com line is `UNIT_MISSING_IN_SOURCE` (4,129,433 lines) and 0 lines have a gram value; Food.com quantities may only be used as counts or presence, never as mass or volume.

The quantity list and the ingredient-part list differ in length in 407,536 of 522,517 recipes (77.995 %), covering 76.823 % of lines, so positional pairing (`recipes.corpus.iter_foodcom`) puts quantities on the wrong food; the proposed rule pairs only equal-length recipes (957,071 lines, 23.177 %) and leaves the rest UNKNOWN.

1,275,153 lines (30.88 %) write fractions with U+2044 FRACTION SLASH, which the frozen quantity parser reads as the digit before the slash only (a count of 1 for 1⁄4, of 3 for 3⁄4); the opt-in SP-002 pre-normaliser changes the normalised amount of 1,275,123 lines and moves rc2 mass-grounded lines from 87 to 127 (Food.com has no units, so mass stays rare); every Food.com quantity figure before the fix carries this caveat.

The ingredient names (4,129,433 mentions, 7,198 distinct phrases) hit the ING/ALIAS lexicon exactly on 82.19 % of mentions and find a lexicon food in 98.89 %; the ING/ALIAS registries are UNVERIFIED, so a hit means the registry has the surface, not a verified identity.

The instruction text has 522,514 texts and 5,275,357 sentences; Rung A tags 8,728,967 ACTION events and maps 76.11 % of the verb-slot words (85.234 % of sentence-initial ones) to a PROC; this is a rule-based coverage count, not an accuracy.
